title: CHAPTER 3: THE HIDDEN CATCH THE PSYCHOLOGY AND SCIENCE TWIST

segments.line: Pip desperately wanted to stop his timer, so he visited a brain
scientist for help. The scientist told him that the timers were tied to how human brains handle fear.
Way back in nineteen eighty-seven, a researcher named Daniel Wegner found a strange brain habit. He called
it ironic process theory, and it happens whenever you try not to fail. When you force yourself not to think about
a white bear, you think about it constantly.
Fighter pilots call this target fixation, and it causes them to crash during fast flight. If
a pilot stares straight at a tall tree, his hands steer right into it.
The floating timers were not reading magic, but measuring the stress inside your own head. As the clock ticks toward zero, your
body floods with four times more stress hormone. That wave
of chemical panic shuts down your memory and makes your hands shake uncontrollably. So the timer does not
predict an accident waiting in the stars for you.
Staring at the glowing numbers is the exact thing that causes you to mess up.
The more you worry about failing, the more likely you are to make it happen.
was creating the very disaster he was trying
